result.topic_en: Gauss sets up a surface parametrized by t and θ, its normal and area element, and the curvature of a curve on the surface: absolute curvature, normal curvature and lateral (geodesic) curvature.
result.transcription:
Die Bestimmende der Fläche [-...-] $t, \theta$
Math 29

$\partial x = a p\,dt + \alpha \pi\,d\theta$ wo $aa+bb+cc=1$
$\partial y = b p\,dt + \beta \pi\,d\theta$ $\alpha\alpha+\beta\beta+\gamma\gamma=1$
$dz = c p\,dt + \gamma \pi\,d\theta$
$\partial x^2+\partial y^2+\partial z^2 = P dt^2 + 2Q\,\partial t\,\partial u + R\,\partial u^2$
$\partial a = x^{(2)}\partial t + x^{(3)} du$
X, Y, Z der Normale angehörig

$\sigma X = (b\gamma - c\beta)$
$\sigma Y = (c\alpha - a\gamma)$
$\sigma Z = (a\beta - \alpha b)$
[-$\sigma = \frac{p\pi \text{ Element der krummen Fläche}}{\partial t\,\partial\theta}$-]
$\sigma p\pi.\partial t.\partial\theta$ = Element der Kr. Fläche
[-...-] $\sigma$ = sin des Winkels um [?] den [-...-] den die Seiten des Elements machen die dem $dt$ und $d\theta$ entsprechen.

Es seien [-...-] $t$ u. $\theta$ functionen von $u$
[-$du = mdt + \mu d\theta$-]

$\frac{dx}{du} = s\xi$ $\frac{d\xi}{du} = \sigma\xi'$
$\frac{dy}{du} = s\eta$ $\frac{d\eta}{dt} = \sigma\eta'$
$\frac{dz}{du} = s\zeta$ $\frac{d\zeta}{dt} = \sigma\eta''$

$\eta\zeta' - \zeta\eta' = \xi''$
$\zeta\xi' - \xi\zeta' = \eta''$
$\xi\eta' - \eta\xi' = \zeta''$

Dann ist
$X\xi + Y\eta + Z\zeta = 0$
$X\xi' + Y\eta' + Z\zeta' = -\cos\psi$
$X\xi'' + Y\eta'' + Z\zeta'' = \sin\psi$

$s\,dt$ Element der Curve
$\sigma du$ Element der Absol: Krümmung
$\frac{\sigma}{s}$ Maass der Absol: Krümm.
$\frac{\sigma}{s}\cos\psi$ Maass der Normal Kr. nach P [?]
$\frac{\sigma}{s}\sin\psi$ Maass der Seitenkr.

$s\xi = a p t' + \alpha\pi\theta'$
$s\eta = b p t' + \beta\pi\theta'$
$s\zeta = c p t' + \gamma\pi\theta'$
[-$ss = aa+bb+cc)$-]
$ss = Pt't' + 2Qt'\theta' + R\theta'\theta'$
$ss' = \frac{\partial P}{\partial t}.t'^3 + \partial 1$

Nun ist

$s'\xi + \xi' s\sigma = a't' + \alpha'\theta' + at'' + \alpha\theta''$
$s'\eta + \eta' s\sigma = b't' + \beta'\theta' + bt'' + \alpha\theta''$
$s'\zeta + \zeta' s\sigma = c't' + \gamma'\theta' + ct'' + \alpha\theta''$

$-\sigma s\cos\psi = [-Xx-] t'^2(Xx^{(2)} + Yy^{(2)} + Zz^{(2)})$
$+ 2t'\theta'(Xx^{(3)} + Yy^{(3)} + Zz^{(3)})$
$+ \theta'\theta'(Xx^{(4)} + Yy^{(4)} + Zz^{(4)})$
